verdictReason: Judged on GEOMETRY (not triangle count — MADR 0050), the TRELLIS single-view bake is NOT better than the parametric source it was conditioned on. Aspect ratio 0.7701 (bake) vs 3.2813 (parametric): the bake is WIDER THAN TALL — the tall/thin IV-pole silhouette is lost. Slimmest vertical slice fraction 0.4408 vs 0.0567: the bake has no sustained thin element (the pole) — a >7x blur. Volume ratio 0.0044 vs 0.0658: the bake is a near-hollow shell (0.0044 of its convex hull filled). Triangle count recorded only: bake 996371 tris vs parametric 284 — NOT a selection criterion. Orchestrator grades the renders: bake lit/structure passes under .openclinxr/evidence/glb-grade-capture/2026-08-10T15-10-00Z/assets/iv-pole/ (front_lit, three_quarter_lit, front_structure, three_quarter_structure) vs the parametric pack renders under .openclinxr/evidence/issue-262/packs/iv_pole_equipment/ (front/side/three_quarter_left/three_quarter_right/back + contact-sheet). NEGATIVE RESULT — closes the parametric-render→TRELLIS equipment route for this evidence. The equipment lane's reference-pack sourcing genuinely depends on an operator decision about image sourcing.

decision.outcome: One subject decides: TRELLIS single-view conditioned on a parametric render does NOT upgrade the geometry — it destroys the defining thin-pole silhouette. The approach is rejected for equipment reference packs.
decision.whatSurvives: The harness capability is general: renderEquipmentReferencePack can produce a 5-view 1024x1024 pack for ANY of the 35 equipment ids in seconds, deterministically, quota-free. That is the reusable factory step; the TRELLIS upgrade leg is the part that failed.
decision.whatTheOperatorDecides: Equipment lane reference-pack sourcing: parametric renders are now the proven deterministic input for anything that consumes 2D reference images; generative image sourcing (Grok Imagine, or an approved alternative) is an operator licensing/provenance decision this slice deliberately did not make.
